title: OmniHealth - SIG walkthrough and evidence planning
topics: Audit logs, retention, and access patterns
Encryption: customer-managed KMS and key rotation
Data residency and private deployment options
summary: Redwood team walked OmniHealth through the SIG v2.0 mapping to Redwood artifacts. Customer focused on SOC2 scope, audit log extraction for Health data flows, and options for customer-managed keys and VPC/private deployments. Action items capture evidence handoff and a short pilot to run CAIQ checks against a sample workload.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Osei (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Security PM), Carlos Mendoza (OmniHealth Head of Security), Neil Carter (Vendor Risk), Asha Patel (Procurement), Tom Nguyen (IT Ops), Dr. Emily Rios (Data Privacy)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, we'll go through the SIG v2, map to our existing artifacts, and then leave time for any evidence questions. Marcus will jump in on the deep technical parts.
[00:18] Carlos Mendoza: Great, thanks. For context, OmniHealth is doing a vendor risk push for our telehealth suite. The big asks are SOC 2 scope, audit logs for any PHI access, and whether we can bring our own keys.
[00:32] Marcus Osei: Yep totally. Quick note — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and we can show how key rotation works. For hosted, there's an option for envelope encryption with customer keys in some regions.
[00:45] Tom Nguyen: When you say "some regions" — we need US-only residency. Is that available for the hosted API or would that force Private?
[00:54] Priya Singh: To clarify, we have region routing policies. Hosted can route to US-only infra but for strict data residency + KMS under customer control, Private or Dedicated with VPC options is the recommended pattern. There's tradeoffs on latency/cost.
[01:10] Neil Carter: On the SIG: we sent a 120-question CAIQ-style form. We don't expect all answers but want to understand where evidence will come from and how quickly you can produce it.
[01:22] Lena Park: Right, we'll map each SIG control to an artifact. We'll call out SOC 2 controls, our architecture diagrams, RBAC docs, SSO integration guides, and sample audit exports. Marcus will flag anything that's more of a process answer vs technical artifact.
[01:35] Marcus Osei: Quick note — on RBAC, Redwood supports granular roles at the token and route level. We do role-based access in the console and via API keys; enterprise customers can tie to SAML groups. There's sometimes a mismatch in how customers want to see 'separation of duties' documented vs how it's implemented.
[01:52] Dr. Emily Rios: How do you handle data deletion and retention for PHI? We need proof that when we request deletion it's actually removed, and audit logs show who requested it.
[02:03] Priya Singh: We have retention policies per environment. For hosted, we retain short-term logs for debugging and then aggregate telemetry; the PHI flow should be scoped out — if PHI must not be stored, we recommend Private deployment or a config that strips PII before persistent storage. We can provide the retention policy doc and deletion runbook as evidence.
[02:20] Carlos Mendoza: Can you produce an extract of audit logs with immutable stamps? Our GRC team wants to see exportable logs for the last 90 days with access events, who accessed keys, etc.
[02:31] Marcus Osei: Yes, audit logs include event types, timestamps, user tokens, and model route. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be pushed to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Logstash) and we can show sample exports. For hosted, we provide redacted audit reports and a logging API.
[02:48] Neil Carter: What's the SOC 2 scope? Specifically, do you include the orchestration layer and third-party GPU providers in scope?
[02:57] Priya Singh: Our SOC 2 report covers our control plane and operational processes. Third-party infra (cloud providers) are disclosed in the report and we provide SOC attestations where available. We can annotate which controls rely on subservice orgs.
[03:12] Asha Patel: Procurement question — do you have a standard BAA? This is healthcare, so we may need HIPAA addendum.
[03:20] Lena Park: We do have HIPAA/BAA templates for enterprise contracts. We'll surface legal team contacts and the standard addendum; customization is possible.
[03:28] [crosstalk, someone muting]
[03:40] Marcus Osei: Back to the SIG mapping: I'll show one example — control SIG-AC-01 (access control). Our artifact is the RBAC matrix doc, console screenshots of role creation, SAML integration guide, and audit log sample showing a user creation event.
[03:58] [04:05] Marcus Osei: I'm going to share a quick link to the RBAC runbook in the chat — (link) — note the runbook includes API snippets for role binding.
[04:20] Tom Nguyen: When you talk about API keys vs SAML: can ops disable keys centrally if someone leaves? We want revocation to be immediate and observable.
[04:31] Marcus Osei: Yes, keys can be revoked via API, and revocation events appear in audit logs. For SAML, mapping to groups is immediate on the next auth exchange; we can show an example where group removal prevents access in under a minute.
[04:47] Carlos Mendoza: On encryption: we need to be able to see who used the key and when. Do you emit key usage logs to customers?
[04:55] Priya Singh: For Dedicated/Private, we can surface KMS usage logs to your logging endpoint. For hosted, we provide summarized key usage reports and are working to expand audited per-call logs where allowed by vendor KMS.
[05:12] Neil Carter: Any limitations with BYOK — e.g., can you re-encrypt existing data if a key is rotated?
[05:19] Marcus Osei: Good question. For models and cached tokens, we use envelope keys, so rotation rotates the envelope. Existing persisted caches are re-wrapped on access. We documented the approach in the KMS FAQ — we'll include that doc.
[05:35] [05:40] Lena Park: Ok, let's go through a set of SIG questions live — we'll read the question and map to artifact and who owns it.
[05:48] [06:00] Marcus Osei: SIG question: "Do you enforce multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts?" Artifact: SSO/SAML configuration + audit logs + MFA policy screenshot. Owner: Priya. Note: for hosted accounts MFA is enforced for the console via SAML with enforced 2FA; API keys don't have MFA but are protected via lifecycle and rotation policies.
[06:25] Carlos Mendoza: It's important for us that admins have MFA enforced and that the policy is auditable.
[06:30] Priya Singh: Understood. We'll mark that as high priority and include a sample audit of admin logins.
[06:40] [07:00] Marcus Osei: SIG question: "Are you encrypting data at rest and in transit?" Answer: yes. Artifacts: TLS cert chain doc, storage encryption doc, KMS configuration screenshots. For at-rest encryption, default is provider-managed keys; BYOK is supported in Private/Dedicated.
[07:20] Tom Nguyen: For our vendor risk, we might require full BYOK plus US-only keys. Is that feasible?
[07:27] Marcus Osei: Yes on Private deployments; for hosted we can sometimes arrange dedicated instances in US regions with customer key wrapping — but it's an enterprise setup. We'll map costs and timeline.
[07:40] [07:45] Lena Park: A note on timelines — Private deployment onboarding is typically 6-8 weeks plus network work. Dedicated reserved capacity can be faster depending on GPU availability. We'll capture options.
[07:58] Neil Carter: On evidence delivery: do you prefer S3 shares, secure portal upload, or an in-console evidence center?
[08:06] Priya Singh: We use a secure evidence portal for SOC and audit docs, and for larger artifacts we do S3 presigned links or direct integration to customer S3. Sensitive items can be delivered via a controlled share with expiration.
[08:20] Carlos Mendoza: Can you show an example of a SOC 2 report redacted? We need to know what's in scope.
[08:25] Lena Park: Yes we'll attach a redacted SOC2 in the follow-up. It will show scope boundaries; we'll call out subservice org dependencies.
[08:36] [09:00] Marcus Osei: SIG control: "Key management" — we'll map to our KMS FAQ, a sample ledger of rotations, and a screenshot of the KMS bindings page. For customer key rotation event, we can show the rewrap flow.
[09:18] Dr. Emily Rios: Regarding audit logs again — do you support immutable storage or WORM for logs? Our compliance requires tamper-evident logs for at least 7 years in some workflows.
[09:30] Priya Singh: We support pushing logs to your immutable storage solution (e.g., S3 with object lock) when on Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we can provide signed exports and a chain-of-custody document but persistent WORM is best done on customer-owned endpoints.
[09:48] Tom Nguyen: Are you able to red-team or provide penetration test evidence?
[09:54] Marcus Osei: We run annual pentests and vulnerability scans; we can provide summary reports and remediation timelines. Full pentest reports are treated as sensitive; we handle them via NDA exchange.
[10:10] [10:30] Marcus Osei: Now, quick demo: I'll show the audit log export flow (screenshare). 
[10:40] [screen shows console navigation noises] 
[11:05] Marcus Osei: Here you can filter by event type — e.g., key_use, token_create, model_invoke — export as JSON or push to S3. You can see an example export in the runbook.
[11:25] Carlos Mendoza: In the sample export, do you include user identifiers that match our SAML names? We need correlation to our identity provider.
[11:33] Marcus Osei: Yes, for SAML-backed users we include the federated identity in the event. For API keys we include the key id and associated service account.
[11:45] Neil Carter: A couple of SIG questions are about "logical separation of tenant data" — how do you prove model cache separation between tenants?
[11:54] Priya Singh: We perform tenancy isolation at runtime via per-tenant namespaces and encryption contexts; we can provide architecture diagrams and test results showing KV cache boundaries. We'll also include a summary of our CI tests that exercise multi-tenant isolation.
[12:10] [12:30] Tom Nguyen: About backups — how long are model caches persisted and could they contain PHI?
[12:37] Marcus Osei: Model KV caches are ephemeral and normally tied to session lifespan; persistent caches are optional and we recommend disabling for PHI workloads. If enabled, they are encrypted and can be scoped to customer-owned keys in Private/Dedicated setups.
[12:55] Carlos Mendoza: On legal evidence: we may ask for employee background checks and SOC control-of-people evidence. Do you have employee attestation artifacts?
[13:05] Lena Park: Yes, HR verification processes and background check policy can be included as redacted HR artifacts. We'll coordinate on minimal necessary evidence.
[13:20] [13:40] Neil Carter: Are there any known gaps in the SIG mapping for healthcare? We need to know up front so our GRC can grade risk correctly.
[13:48] Priya Singh: There are a few items that commonly require customer process alignment — e.g., end-to-end PHI minimization (we can provide tooling but customers must avoid sending raw PHI for hosted workflows), and long-term WORM logs for regulatory retention — these are addressable but often require Dedicated/Private and customer-side storage. We'll mark those as expected mitigations.
[14:12] Asha Patel: When you provide the SIG mapping, can you highlight which artifacts are "documents" vs "config screenshots" vs "process attestations"? That makes it easier for our vendor risk team.
[14:22] Lena Park: Absolutely yes we'll categorize each artifact and provide a confidence level and delivery method (portal link / sample export / onsite attestation).
[14:35] [15:00] Marcus Osei: Ok quick demo of KMS binding: (screen noise) here we're showing a customer-managed KMS binding in a Dedicated cluster. You can see the key alias and last rotation timestamp.
[15:20] Tom Nguyen: For BYOK can we supply an external HSM?
[15:26] Marcus Osei: We support HSM-backed keys when deploying in Private with network peering to your HSM endpoints, yes. There are network/security design considerations though.
[15:38] Neil Carter: Any special compliance packages for healthcare — e.g., HIPAA scoping in SOC 2 or supplemental attestation?
[15:46] Priya Singh: We have a HIPAA readiness package and BAA as mentioned. The SOC 2 report doesn't explicitly say "HIPAA" but we provide artifact tie-ins and the BAA covers the obligations.
[16:00] [16:30] Carlos Mendoza: On the CAIQ overlap — can you provide a prefilled CAIQ response set so we don't have to start from scratch?
[16:37] Lena Park: Yes we'll include a prefilled CAIQ with references to docs and screenshots. It won't be the full set but a prioritized, annotated subset for healthcare controls.
[16:50] Neil Carter: When you say "prefilled" — do you mark which are "attested" vs "in-progress"? We need to show our risk panel which items are mitigated not just answered.
[17:00] Priya Singh: We'll add a status column per control: "evidence provided", "process attestation", "requires customer config", and "require private deployment".
[17:12] [17:40] Marcus Osei: A quick note about performance tests — we'll run a light benchmark for the pilot and include latency/cost profiles so you can see impact of encryption layer and private routing.
[17:55] Tom Nguyen: Are there additional costs for pushing logs to our S3 or for BYOK?
[18:02] Lena Park: BYOK and Private deployments have separate pricing lines. Log forwarding is usually included but long-term storage costs are passed through. We'll provide a pricing appendix in the follow-up.
[18:18] Neil Carter: Ok next — evidence delivery and NDA. We prefer evidence portal with expiring links. Also we'll probably need the pentest report under NDA.
[18:28] Lena Park: Yep we'll route pentest reports under NDA and use the portal for normal artifacts.
[18:36] [19:00] Marcus Osei: Wrapping up: action items — I'll compile the SIG mapping and call out redactions. Priya will add security-runbook artifacts. Lena will push the SOC redacted doc and contract/Baa templates.
[19:18] Carlos Mendoza: One last question — for auditability, do you store who performed administrative operations in the database itself or only in logs? We need to correlate alerts to DB changes.
[19:28] Priya Singh: We capture both: operational events are in the audit log and configuration changes are captured in an immutable config ledger for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we provide ledger exports.
[19:44] Asha Patel: Procurement timeline — assuming pilot ok, we may need a 90-day procurement window. Is that supported?
[19:51] Lena Park: Many enterprise deals go through that cadence. We'll coordinate with your procurement and legal teams.
[20:00] [20:30] Closing remarks and recap.
[20:40] Lena Park: Recap: Redwood to send prefilled CAIQ + redacted SOC 2 + annotated SIG mapping. Customer to send prioritized CAIQ questions and data flows. Next meeting: technical SAML/KMS demo and audit-log export test.
[20:58] Carlos Mendoza: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[21:05] Meeting ends.
